title: Introducing a Smarter Start: Two Start Areas and a Wave System for the 2025 Sanlam Cape Town Marathon
claims: The event introduced two start areas and a five-wave system to reduce batch loading congestion, congestion in the first 10 km, and pressure on the finish line.
The Stadium start on Fritz Sonnenberg Road remains for elites and a large portion of the field, while the Beach Road start is on Beach Road in Mouille Point.

Runners are seeded into batches A–N; the yellow wave is batches A–D at the Stadium, pink is G–H at the Stadium, red is K–N at the Stadium, blue is E–F at the Beach Road start, and green is I–J at the Beach Road start.
Crowd Science used the route GPX, road-width data, historical congestion data and pinch points including Stanhope Road and the Company Gardens to model the two-start system.
Wave timing is calculated so the last runner in each wave is beyond the convergence point at Fritz Sonnenberg Road and Beach Road before the next wave starts.
The race clock runs for 6 hours 30 minutes from the time the final runner crosses the start mat, and cut-off times are calculated on that basis.
The marathon is mat-to-mat timed for all participants except elites.
In the 2025 plan the first yellow wave departed the Stadium at 06:17 and the first blue wave departed Beach Road at 06:31.
